claims.text: At stage-2 Order declares `public string Status { get; private set; }`; CustomerId, PlacedAt and Items also have private setters.
A private set accessor lets only code inside the class assign the property, while the public get lets any code read it.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: Restricting accessor accessibility; Properties

claims.text: MarkPaid() throws already-cancelled for cancelled, already-paid for any other non-new status, else sets paid; Cancel() throws already-cancelled/already-shipped, else sets cancelled; Ship() throws already-cancelled, already-shipped, or not-paid when not paid, else sets shipped.

Given the four statuses allowed by the orders table (new, paid, shipped, cancelled), the allowed changes are exactly new->paid (MarkPaid), paid->shipped (Ship), new->cancelled and paid->cancelled (Cancel); a refused change leaves Status unchanged.

claims.text: PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/ship carries [Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")] and its action only calls OrderService.ShipOrderAsync, which finds the order (KeyNotFoundException if missing), calls order.Ship(), notifier.Send, then SaveChangesAsync; neither has a role or status check.
The StaffOnly policy runs before the action, so a caller without the staff role gets 403 (401 with no token) and ShipOrderAsync never runs; the policy does not look at the order.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: policy-based authorization, [Authorize] runs before the action; backend.l2.role-based-access (approved)

claims.text: A staff request to the ship endpoint for a cancelled order passes the policy, Ship() throws OrderStatusException already-cancelled, and ExceptionHandlingMiddleware answers 409 with a type ending in already-cancelled.
An enum limits which values exist, not which value may follow which: any code that can assign an enum property can assign any of its members.
Code inside Order can still assign any status through the private setter; a method that sets Status = "shipped" with no check compiles and nothing refuses it.
claims.source_hint: C# docs: accessibility of private members (accessible within the containing type)

claims.text: Reading Order alone lists every status change the application's code can make (mark paid, ship, cancel); at stage-1 the two assignments sat as plain lines in OrderService's methods with no check of the starting status.
Two requests changing the same order at once are caught at save time by the Version (xmin) concurrency token, not by the status methods.
